metadata.case_name: YANG YI CHAI v. CHENG KAM SHING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Director of a company whose business was concerned with Chinese antiques and works of art; solely responsible for the purchase of goods for the company and was consulted by customers for his expert opinion; travelled to Mainland China and to the U.S.A. to attend auctions.

injuries.description: the Plaintiff suffered a fracture of the neck of the right femur.
source: the Plaintiff suffered a fracture of the neck of the right femur.
an operation known as an 'Austin Moore' Replacement Arthroplasty was carried out, in lay terms this was the replacement of the human bone at the head of femur by a stainless steel device.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of neck of femur, unspecified

manifestations.description: slight discomfort and pain over the right hip after walking for 20 minutes
a ½ inch shortening of his right leg
slight limitation in internal and external rotation of the right hip joint
He can walk for little more than 10 minutes and after standing for 10 minutes he has to sit down and rest.
20% permanent disability resulting from the injury (opinion of Dr Chien)

treatments_received: Admitted to Queen Elizabeth Hospital on 19th November, 1982
an operation known as an 'Austin Moore' Replacement Arthroplasty was carried out, in lay terms this was the replacement of the human bone at the head of femur by a stainless steel device.
nursing care provided by International Nursing Service Ltd.

losses.description: Pain Suffering and Loss of Amenities

comparable_cases.injury_description: In that case, the injuries were more extensive than in the present case, although medical opinion assessed the Plaintiff's disability at 20%.
Disability of 20% (details unclear from the report); Judge appeared to have awarded about $55,000.
